modelVerification: explicit invocation only; CLI did not echo model

findings.message: Anchor the placeholder alternative at the beginning of the input. Its missing ^ allows IDs that do not start with aws:/// to pass validation.
findings.evidence: For xaws:///us-east-1a/i-placeholder-abc, FindStringSubmatch matches the aws:/// suffix through the second alternative. Parsing then returns Name="us-east-1a" without an error because id[7:] includes the extra leading slash. Previously both alternatives began with ^ and rejected this input.

findings.message: Preserve the complete placeholder name after the zone separator. Taking only splitted[1] discards subsequent slashes and their contents, violating the placeholder-name contract.
findings.evidence: For aws:///us-east-1a/i-placeholder-abc/part, validation succeeds, but the returned Name is i-placeholder-abc instead of i-placeholder-abc/part. The previous placeholder capture retained the full suffix. Local callers pass this altered reference to GetAsgForInstance and InstanceStatus; their implementations are unavailable.

result.coverage: Inspected TASK.json, CHANGE.diff, the complete staged source, and all local parser callers. Compared both regex alternatives and name extraction with the original implementation. Ordinary-name optional suffix handling remains equivalent, and ProviderID is preserved unchanged.
limitations: No tests were run; examples were evaluated by source inspection.
Manager and cache implementations are not supplied, so downstream lookup, status, and deletion consequences cannot be established.
result.contribution: Established two independent contract regressions with concrete inputs and before/after behavior. Excluded unchanged ordinary-name suffix handling and limited downstream claims to evidenced reference propagation.
